title: Hot-swap a server's failed power supply without disturbing the live one
instruction: The power supply with the amber light has failed. Replace it with the spare power supply on the table, without disturbing the power supply with the green light, which is keeping the server running.
context: Data-center technicians replace failed redundant (N+1) server power supplies while the server keeps running on the other one. On a CRPS supply the release tab beside the fixed handle has to be squeezed toward the handle while pulling, and the long, heavy new unit has to be pushed in square and firmly enough to mate its edge connector (tens of newtons) until its latch catches, without knocking the live unit or its power cord.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). Power-supply cage: grey sheet steel (or PLA), fixed to the table, two bays side by side facing the arms with their mouths at x 36.95, each 7.75 cm wide, 4.05 cm tall under a 0.4 cm roof and 18.4 cm deep from the mouth to a back stop, separated by a 1.5 cm divider; the left bay is centred on y 0 and the right on y -9.25. Each side wall has a 1.5 cm lead-in plate at the mouth, flared 30 degrees. The server body continues 13.1 cm behind the back stop. In the left wall of each bay, 0.9 to 2.65 cm inside the mouth and 1.3 to 2.7 cm above the table, is a 1.75 x 1.4 cm notch. Connector: from the back stop of each bay a steel blade (0.3 cm thick, 2 cm tall, 0.6 cm above the table) reaches 1.55 cm forward on the bay's centreline, with a ridge on each side standing 0.35 cm proud, its crest 0.8 cm in front of the back stop, its front face at 50 degrees and its back face at 40 degrees. Three identical CRPS power supplies, black, 18.5 x 7.35 x 3.95 cm, 0.9 kg, with a status light and an AC inlet low on the right of the face. Each has an orange grip handle fixed to its face: a vertical bar (1 x 0.8 x 4.8 cm) on two arms 2.75 cm in front of the face, just right of the centreline (y 0 to -0.8 cm). 0.6 cm left of the bar stands a separate green release tab (1 x 0.8 x 4.8 cm, 60 g with its latch) that slides 0.5 cm toward the handle against a 1 N per mm spring and stops 0.1 cm short of it; it draws in a hook on the supply's left side. At rest the hook's square catch (0.4 x 0.5 x 1.2 cm, 1.25 cm behind the face) stands 0.5 cm out of the side into the bay wall's notch; behind it a ramp, cresting 0.1 cm higher, slopes back to the side at 27 degrees. In a 1.6 x 3 cm slot at the back of each supply, two sprung steel contacts (0.3 x 0.4 x 2 cm, 0.6 cm apart, 5 N per mm each) take the blade: pushing a supply home spreads them 0.2 cm over its ridge during the last 0.8 cm (a mating force of about 35 N), and they drop behind it 0.1 cm before home. The failed supply (amber light) is latched in the left bay and the live supply (green light) in the right bay, each face 0.2 cm proud of its mouth; the spare (no light) lies on the table with its centre at x 23.5, y 22, face toward the arms. Power cords: the live supply's cord plug (black, 3.75 x 1.8 x 1.6 cm, IEC C13) sits in the AC inlet on the right of its face and moves with it; the cord beyond it is not modelled (taken as routed away along the rack). The failed supply's cord has already been unplugged, as the first step of a swap; the spare has none. In a real-world build nothing is powered or connected to mains: the supplies are unpowered (or empty weighted shells) and the plug is a dummy plug on a short cut cord. Fabrication files, parts list and assembly: fabrication/BUILD.md.
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a top photo; positions from where a supply sits latched home in the left bay. 0 if the live (green) supply was at any point moved more than 5 mm. Otherwise: 1.0 once all of the following have held together for 1 s: the spare is home in the left bay (within 1.5 mm along it and 2 mm across it, level within 3 degrees) with its hook out in the notch (release tab within 1 mm of its rest position), the failed supply is clear of the bay (back face at least 5 mm in front of the mouth, or its centre more than 7.85 cm to the side), and the spare is still (it moved less than 1 mm over the preceding 1 s). Until then (and if it never holds for 1 s): 0.75 if, after the failed supply came out, the spare was pushed in with its back face 10 cm inside the mouth; 0.5 if the failed supply was pulled all the way out (back face 5 mm in front of the mouth); 0.25 if it was pulled at least 2 cm out; else 0.
reset_notes: Push the failed supply back into the left bay until its hook snaps into the notch; put the spare back on its marked outline. The live supply is not moved.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; supplies at full CRPS size and weight. Fixed handle with a separate sprung release tab (5 N) driving a ramped hook. Edge connector: sprung contacts ride over a ridge on a blade in the last 8 mm (about 35 N to mate, 11 N to unmate; CRPS card-edge spec: up to 40 N); contacts on the supply, blade in the cage. Handle enlarged for gripper fingers; 2 mm bay clearance; cage fixed. Live supply's cord: plug only. Nothing is powered.
